open_points.subject: ProofResult representation of constant failures
open_points.text: A05 says “the first check that fails is the result, with its phase, its node or edge and its reason”, but phase 2 can fail on a constant, while M17 and State 0 allow only “the first failing edge or node”.
open_points.question: How is a phase-2 constant failure represented in ProofResult?
options: Add constants as a possible failure subject
Report the constant's target node
Refuse all such faults during composition instead
open_points.default_guess: Report the target node and identify the constant in the reason.

open_points.subject: Ordering edges with equal endpoint keys
open_points.text: Edges are ordered by “(`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`)”, although two edges with those same fields may have different guards.
open_points.question: What orders edges whose endpoint tuples are equal but whose guard fields differ?
options: Extend the order with guard port and guard value
Preserve submitted order
Treat equal endpoint tuples as an unordered set
open_points.default_guess: Extend the order with the canonical JSON of the guard, with an absent guard first.

open_points.subject: Ordering constants with the same target
open_points.text: Constants are checked “by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”, but multiple constants may target the same port and are not rejected until phase 6.
open_points.question: What orders same-target constants when one fails an earlier phase and another does not?
options: Extend the order with the constant's canonical content
Preserve submitted order
Reject repeated constant targets during composition
open_points.default_guess: Extend the order with the constant's canonical content.

open_points.subject: Selecting the reported fan-in conflict
open_points.text: Phase 6 says “no two edges that can both deliver ... end at the same port”, but its order is only “by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”.
open_points.question: When three or more edges conflict at the first port, which edge or pair is named as the failure?
options: Name only the destination port
Name the first conflicting pair under a complete edge order
Name every conflicting edge
open_points.default_guess: Name the first conflicting pair under a complete edge order.

open_points.subject: Flow identity sorting for tied edges and constants
open_points.text: A01 sorts “edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”, but those keys can tie for distinct edges or constants.
open_points.question: How are distinct tied items ordered before hashing a flow version?
options: Add all remaining meaning facts as canonical tie-breakers
Keep request order for tied items
Refuse tied items before computing identity
open_points.default_guess: Use each item's complete canonical JSON as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: Contract port validation order when names tie across directions
open_points.text: A02 checks failures across ports, while input and output ports may legally have the same name and A16 only falls back to the smallest identifier.
open_points.question: If equally named input and output ports fail different checks in the same phase, which failure is first?
options: Order ports by (`direction`, `name`)
Check all inputs before all outputs
Check all outputs before all inputs
open_points.default_guess: Order ports by (`direction`, `name`), matching A01.

open_points.subject: Media-type validity
open_points.text: A02 requires that “a `file` port declares exactly one media type”, but no rule says what syntax or characters constitute a media type.
open_points.question: Which media-type strings are valid, particularly before they are emitted as HTTP Content-Type values?
options: Require a defined RFC media-type grammar
Accept any bounded nonempty string
Require only lowercase type/subtype without parameters
open_points.default_guess: Require a syntactically valid type/subtype without parameters or control characters.

open_points.subject: Sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”, while A03 supplies “one private exchange directory” and permits opening any path inside that directory and the read-only runtime.
open_points.question: May function code read runtime files and create arbitrary scratch files in the exchange directory, or may it access only explicitly supplied input and output files?
options: Allow runtime reads and bounded private scratch
Allow only designated input/output paths
Treat any direct filesystem access as a sandbox violation
open_points.default_guess: Allow the read-only runtime plus bounded private scratch because A03 is the more specific rule.

open_points.subject: Completeness of the no-clock rule
open_points.text: A03 claims “every clock ... entry point” is replaced and State 0 says functions have “no clock”, but the closed list omits clock-bearing APIs such as `time.clock_gettime`, `os.times`, and filesystem metadata timestamps.
open_points.question: Is the stated closed trap list authoritative even though other standard-library clock observations remain, or must every clock-observing API be blocked?
options: The written list is authoritative and these APIs remain usable
Expand isolation to block every clock observation
Remove clock-bearing modules and metadata from the runtime
open_points.default_guess: Block every clock observation and expand the release's closed list accordingly.

open_points.subject: Detection of caught resource-limit failures
open_points.text: A03 says “a limit hit ... `resource_exhausted`” even though `setrlimit` failures such as allocation or process creation errors can be caught by user code, with no specified parent-visible hit record.
open_points.question: What observable event proves that memory, process, or scratch limits were hit when user code catches the resulting error and returns valid output?
options: Instrument and report every denied limit operation
Classify only externally observable termination or measured excess
Allow a caught limit error to succeed
open_points.default_guess: Instrument denied resource operations so the parent records a limit hit even if caught.

open_points.subject: Cleanup failure versus normal outcome precedence
open_points.text: Rule 5 makes the outcome the first of timeout, resource exhaustion, sandbox violation, crash, contract violation and success, while rule 7 says any unconfirmed cleanup is recorded `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`.
open_points.question: If cleanup is unconfirmed after a timeout, limit hit, or sandbox violation, which outcome is recorded?
options: `crashed` with `cleanup_failed` overrides every earlier outcome
Keep the rule-5 outcome and stop the kernel
Apply rule-5 precedence and use `cleanup_failed` only when no earlier outcome exists
open_points.default_guess: Record `crashed` with `cleanup_failed` because the output is discarded and the kernel stops.

open_points.subject: Printed-output resource behavior
open_points.text: A03 bounds returned outputs and retains no stdout, but says only “Nothing the code prints ... is interpreted” and gives no limit or handling rule for stdout or stderr produced by untrusted code.
open_points.question: How are stdout and stderr drained and bounded, and what outcome results when code writes without limit?
options: Discard through bounded nonblocking sinks and classify excess as `resource_exhausted`
Redirect both to `/dev/null`
Let pipe backpressure eventually cause `timeout`
open_points.default_guess: Redirect stdout and stderr to a sink that stores nothing and cannot block or grow.

open_points.subject: Trial execution failure detail
open_points.text: A03 says “The kernel keeps at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it as `failure_detail`” for every function execution, but TrialExecution M07 has no `failure_detail` field.
open_points.question: Where is the bounded exception type and message stored for a trial or admission execution?
options: Add `failure_detail` to TrialExecution
Keep details only for run NodeExecutions
Return the detail transiently but do not persist it
open_points.default_guess: Add the same bounded `failure_detail` to TrialExecution.

open_points.subject: Completeness of expected trial outputs
open_points.text: M06 allows `expected_outputs` to be absent, while A04 says expected outputs “when present, fit the output ports” and later compares “every output's digest” with the expected one.
open_points.question: When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every output port, or may it specify only a subset?
options: Require exactly all output ports
Allow a subset and compare only named outputs
Allow missing ports to mean only schema validation
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all output ports.

open_points.subject: Meaning of an earlier implementation for rollback
open_points.text: Rollback “activates an earlier implementation” that has a current-corpus admitted verdict, but “earlier” is not defined.
open_points.question: May rollback select any admitted implementation of the current contract version, or only one submitted earlier than the current implementation or previously activated?
options: Any non-current admitted implementation
Only an implementation previously active
Only an implementation submitted before the current one
open_points.default_guess: Allow any non-current implementation admitted over the current corpus.

open_points.subject: Failed configuration reread state
open_points.text: A16 compares the configuration bytes with “the last read”; on a failed reread “the old list is not kept”, and every request is refused “until a re-read passes”.
open_points.question: After an invalid changed file is read, is its digest remembered, and what causes the unchanged file to be parsed again or a repaired file with identical bytes to be noticed?
options: Remember a failed state and parse on every request until success
Keep only the last successfully parsed digest
Remember the invalid digest and retry only when bytes change
open_points.default_guess: Enter a failed state and parse the file on every request until a valid token list is obtained.

open_points.subject: Credential trailing-newline removal
open_points.text: A17 defines the credential as UTF-8 content “without one trailing newline”.
open_points.question: Does this remove one LF, one CRLF sequence, every trailing line break, or exactly one Unicode newline character?
options: Remove exactly one terminal LF and an immediately preceding CR
Remove exactly one terminal LF only
Strip all trailing newline sequences
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one terminal LF and an immediately preceding CR if present.

open_points.subject: Meaning of control character in header values
open_points.text: A17 rejects a credential containing “a control character”, and A08 uses the same phrase for required-header values, without defining the character set.
open_points.question: Which code points count as control characters, and are non-ASCII header values permitted on the wire?
options: Reject ASCII CTLs and DEL and require visible ASCII
Reject every Unicode General Category Cc character
Apply the HTTP field-value byte grammar after UTF-8 encoding
open_points.default_guess: Require visible ASCII plus permitted horizontal space, rejecting CTLs and DEL.

open_points.subject: Symlink-safe opening of the installation configuration
open_points.text: The configuration “must be a regular file, not a symbolic link”, but unlike secret files and data-directory files the text does not require opening it without following symbolic links or bind the check to the opened file descriptor.
open_points.question: How must the kernel prevent a check/open race or a symlinked parent from substituting the configuration file?
options: Open with no-follow semantics and validate the opened descriptor
Perform a path check before an ordinary open
Trust the host to prevent path replacement
open_points.default_guess: Open with no-follow semantics and validate ownership, mode, and regular-file status on the opened descriptor.

open_points.subject: Meaning of a private data directory
open_points.text: A18 says “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise” without defining ownership, permission bits, or ACL treatment.
open_points.question: What exact ownership and permission conditions must the data directory and its contents satisfy?
options: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permission on every entry
Require only that the top directory is mode 0700
Accept any permissions when the effective user can access the files
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permission on the directory and every contained entry.

open_points.subject: Timestamp sampling within one action
open_points.text: A19 says every timestamp comes from one clock module, but does not say when or how often that clock is sampled when one request or store call writes several related records.
open_points.question: Do related records share one request timestamp, receive separate readings, or use specified event-boundary readings?
options: One timestamp per request
One timestamp per store transaction
A separate reading at each named event such as start, decision, send and conclusion
open_points.default_guess: Read the clock separately at each semantically named event.

open_points.subject: Pinned dependency versions for release v1
open_points.text: A20 says “A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of the sandbox runtime”, but the text supplies no dependency list or versions and names only “CPython 3.12”.
open_points.question: What exact dependency set, CPython patch/build, bubblewrap version, and other sandbox-runtime artifacts constitute release v1?
options: List exact versions and hashes in the accepted release text
Define v1 as dependency-free except CPython and bubblewrap, with exact versions
Leave selection to the implementation build lockfile
open_points.default_guess: Define the exact versions and hashes in a release manifest treated as part of A20.

open_points.subject: Required security-review categories
open_points.text: A21 defines completeness using “every_required_category_has_one_outcome”, but nowhere defines the authoritative set of required categories.
open_points.question: Against what closed category list can the security gate verify that the review is complete rather than merely verifying the categories that happen to be present?
options: Declare a closed required-category enumeration
Reference a versioned external security-review standard
Treat the displayed categories as the complete required set
open_points.default_guess: Declare the displayed categories as an explicit closed required-category enumeration.

open_points.subject: Flow activation pinned by a run
open_points.text: A12 says a run pins only “the flow version” and function implementations, while M26 and A10 require a draft-write attempt to name “the flow activation under which the run started”.
open_points.question: How does a run unambiguously retain the exact FlowActivation record when the same version may have multiple activation records?
options: Store the FlowActivation store position in Run
Derive the last activation preceding the Run record in store order
Use only the flow version and do not distinguish repeated activations
open_points.default_guess: Store the exact FlowActivation store position in the Run.

open_points.subject: Ordering ready executions against derived skip and upstream-failure records
open_points.text: A13 defines the next ready node and A15 orders records for nodes that become non-executable together, but neither orders a ready node against a node that has just become `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`.
open_points.question: When both kinds of work are available, are non-executable records written before executing the next ready node, after it, or interleaved by node identifier?
options: Treat all ready and conclusively non-executable nodes in one node-id order
Write every newly derivable skip/failure record first
Execute ready nodes first, then write derived records
open_points.default_guess: Use one node-id order across executable and conclusively non-executable nodes.

open_points.subject: Resources on an empty mapped function execution record
open_points.text: A13 requires a mapped node over an empty list to write a successful NodeExecution naming what it pins, although no sandbox execution occurs; M23 says `resources_used` is “for a function node”.
open_points.question: Is `resources_used` absent, zero-valued, or otherwise represented on the empty-map record of a function node?
options: Absent because no function execution occurred
Present with all counters zero
Present with the resources used by list handling outside the sandbox
open_points.default_guess: Make it absent because the sandbox did not run.

open_points.subject: Size of the repair trace window
open_points.text: A15 says repair returns “the latest NodeExecutions ... at most `page_size_max` of them” but does not choose a count or say that the caller chooses one.
open_points.question: How many recent NodeExecutions does the repair inspection return by default, and can it be paged or sized?
options: Use `page_size_default` with normal list pagination
Always return exactly up to `page_size_max`
Let the caller request a bounded count
open_points.default_guess: Use `page_size_default` and the A16 pagination convention.

open_points.subject: Manifest structural validity
open_points.text: A08 checks whether the record is valid JSON and whether it “lacks `service` or `capabilities`”, but does not define required JSON types and shapes for the record, capability entries, instances, required headers, or their members.
open_points.question: Which malformed manifest shapes are rejected, and where do those failures fall in the rule-5 first-failure order?
options: Define a complete manifest schema and ordered validation rules
Treat every unexpected shape as invalid JSON
Let field access failures become a generic manifest mismatch
open_points.default_guess: Define and validate a complete manifest schema before semantic checks.

open_points.subject: Duplicate member names in manifest JSON
open_points.text: State 1 says a duplicate JSON key is refused wherever it enters because JCS cannot represent it, while A08's ordered manifest-mismatch checks do not mention duplicate member names.
open_points.question: Are duplicate member names a JSON parse failure, a separate manifest mismatch, or accepted according to the parser's duplicate-key behavior?
options: Reject them as invalid JSON
Add an ordered duplicate-member manifest check
Accept the parser's selected value
open_points.default_guess: Reject them as invalid JSON before any field checks.

open_points.subject: Missing or non-text idempotency_key
open_points.text: A08 says `idempotency_key` is `null` or otherwise “the text split on `+`”, but gives no outcome when the field is absent or has a non-string, non-null value.
open_points.question: What does a missing or wrongly typed `idempotency_key` mean for read and non-read operations?
options: Reject it as a manifest mismatch
Treat absence as `null`
Ignore its type for read operations but reject it otherwise
open_points.default_guess: Require the field and reject any value other than null or string.

open_points.subject: Supported schemas on binding ports
open_points.text: M01 says every port schema is in the kernel's supported subset, but A08 borrows only selected A02 port rules and does not clearly require binding input and output schemas to be in that subset.
open_points.question: Must every binding port schema pass the same supported-subset validation as a contract port, and at what point in rule 5 is that checked?
options: Yes, before request-shape checks
Yes, after request-shape checks
No; arbitrary schemas are allowed on bindings
open_points.default_guess: Require the supported subset before applying request-shape checks.

open_points.subject: Allowed api_base_url form
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host, while A09 joins it by removing a trailing slash and appending the operation path.
open_points.question: May `api_base_url` contain userinfo, a query, fragment, non-root path, percent escapes, or multiple trailing slashes, and how are those cases joined?
options: Restrict it to scheme, host, optional port and optional path prefix without query, fragment or userinfo
Use standard RFC URL resolution
Append the declared path to the raw URL string exactly as described
open_points.default_guess: Allow a path prefix but forbid userinfo, query and fragment, then define exact concatenation.

open_points.subject: Meaning of loopback host
open_points.text: A09 permits plain HTTP when the `api_base_url` “host is a loopback address” without saying whether this is a literal-address check or a DNS-resolution check.
open_points.question: Do `localhost`, a hostname resolving to loopback, IPv4-mapped IPv6, and alternate textual loopback forms qualify?
options: Only an IP literal classified as loopback
Any hostname whose resolved address set is entirely loopback
The literal names `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `::1` only
open_points.default_guess: Require an IP literal that the standard IP parser classifies as loopback.

open_points.subject: Multipart field-name and filename escaping
open_points.text: Multipart parts use `name="<port>"` and `filename="<port>"`, while port names have no stated HTTP-token grammar or escaping rule.
open_points.question: How are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII text, CR/LF, and other special characters in port names encoded or refused?
options: Restrict multipart-capable port names to a safe ASCII token grammar
Define quoted-string escaping and extended filename encoding
Insert bounded port text verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Restrict multipart-capable port names to a safe ASCII token grammar.

open_points.subject: Multipart boundary selection and collision handling
open_points.text: A09 defines multipart parts, and A10 excludes the boundary as kernel framing, but neither defines how a boundary is chosen or ensures it does not occur in part content.
open_points.question: How is the multipart boundary generated, and what happens if its delimiter occurs in an input part?
options: Choose a deterministic content-derived boundary and verify non-collision
Choose a random boundary and regenerate until collision-free
Use a fixed release boundary and escape content
open_points.default_guess: Choose a random boundary and regenerate until it is absent from every part body.

open_points.subject: Encoding required HTTP header values
open_points.text: Required-header values are sent “verbatim”, although A08 permits values beyond a vaguely excluded set of control characters and does not define a byte encoding.
open_points.question: Which byte encoding and HTTP field-value grammar turns a manifest string into the exact header sent and included in an approval?
options: Require visible ASCII and send those bytes
Encode Unicode as UTF-8 bytes
Use the HTTP client's native header encoding
open_points.default_guess: Require visible ASCII and send exactly those bytes.

open_points.subject: Transport timeout interval
open_points.text: A09 requires a response to arrive within `transport_timeout_ms`, while A19 calls it the deadline of one HTTP request, without defining its start and completion events.
open_points.question: Does the timeout cover DNS, connection, TLS, request upload, response headers, and the complete response body, and when exactly does it start and stop?
options: One total deadline from before DNS until the complete bounded body is read
Start after connection and stop at final response headers
Use separate per-phase timeouts each equal to the ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Use one total monotonic deadline from before DNS until the complete response body has been read or rejected.

open_points.subject: Draft-write authority after repeated activation
open_points.text: A10 requires a draft-write attempt to record “the FlowActivation M18 of the run's version”, but a version can have several distinct activation records and Run does not name one.
open_points.question: Which activation is recorded when the same flow version was activated, replaced, and activated again before or during the run?
options: The exact activation current when the run started
The earliest activation of that version
The latest activation of that version at send time
open_points.default_guess: Record the exact activation current when the run started.
